primary_topics: Eulogy delivered at the first-night wake of Dr. George S.K. Ty (Dr. George), Founder and Chairman of the Metrobank Group, on November 24, 2018 -- the night of his death
Nine personal stories illustrating Dr. Ty's character: integrity, generosity, visionary leadership, discipline, meekness, trustworthiness, discipline, and dedication to duty

Dr. Ty's philanthropic philosophy: 10% of total wealth to philanthropy (vs. the standard corporate 2% of net income); founding of the Toyota Institute of Technology (P1 billion matched by Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda of Japan); building the Mary the Queen Catholic Church in Nanjing; donating to the Manila Cathedral restoration

CJP's relationship with Dr. Ty: ~20 years, from meeting as Board of Judges chair for Metrobank's Outstanding Teachers search, to Senior Adviser of Metrobank, to Chairman of Metrobank Foundation's Board of Advisers
sub_topics: CJP was shocked by the news: Nick Torres called while CJP was seated beside President Duterte at the San Beda function at Club Filipino in San Juan; had to text Cardinal Tagle (in Hong Kong) to request him to celebrate tonight's Mass; Tagle celebrated the Mass and delivered a homily; CJP skipped receiving the FEU Law Alumni 'Diamond Jubilee Tamaraw Award' (given only once every 50 years) to attend; daughter Tet received the award in his stead

Story 1 -- Outstanding Teachers Search: CJP was invited to be a member, then chairman, of the Board of Judges for the Metrobank Foundation's Search for the 10 Outstanding Teachers; Dr. Ty was always present on a side chair, patiently listening, never intruding; CJP's pointed question to one teacher: 'If the Bank is not getting anything from you... why do you think Metrobank will reward you generously?' The soft smile of Dr. Ty affirmed it touched his 'altruistic heart'; 'He never asked from, or was given any favor by, me as a sitting member of the Supreme Court. Our friendship flourished purely on mutual respect and genuine brotherly affection.'

Story 2 -- Senior Adviser and Board Chair: after CJP's judicial retirement, Dr. Ty invited him as Senior Adviser of Metrobank and Board of Advisers member of Metrobank Foundation; after CJ Cory Aquino died (August 1, 2009), Dr. Ty invited CJP to replace her as Chair of the Board of Advisers; CJP remonstrated and was persuaded to accept

Story 3 -- The golf chastisement: at a lunch at the Penthouse of GT Tower, CJP whispered to Dr. Ty how impressed he was with Alfred's golf game; Dr. Ty summoned Alfred and told him: 'The Chief Justice told me that you are a very good golfer. That is bad. It means you are often in the golf course and not giving enough time to your work.' CJP was embarrassed and later told Alfred: 'I am sorry I put you in trouble. Since then, I stopped playing with him, lest I slipped and put him in trouble again.'

Story 4 -- BPI invitation: Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala invited CJP to BPI despite knowing his Metrobank connection; CJP phoned Dr. Ty who insisted on coming to CJP's home instead; after hearing about the BPI invitation over the phone, Dr. Ty said immediately: 'Please accept the offer. I fully trust you. I know you will never reveal any business secret, whether of Metrobank or of BPI or of anyone.' -- explains CJP's dual role in both largest Philippine banks

Story 5 -- APEC Toyota Innova gift: after APEC 2015, Toyota was selling discounted vehicles; CJP asked Alfred whether the FLP could buy a used Toyota Innova for the secretariat; a week later, Dr. Ty visited CJP at home and brought a brand-new red Innova -- not a used one, and already registered in FLP's name; 'such is his unsolicited generosity for worthy causes'

Story 6 -- 10% wealth to philanthropy: Dr. Ty wanted to donate 10% of his wealth to philanthropy (vs. corporate standard of 2% of net income); set aside one billion pesos for the Toyota Institute of Technology; at a private dinner hosted by Dr. Ty for Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda (retired Toyota Japan Chairman), CJP asked why Toyota yielded majority control in the Philippines while retaining control everywhere else; Toyoda explained: 'it was only in the Philippines that Toyota had consistently topped all other motor vehicle brands for 27 consecutive years. Not even in Japan has such a record been equaled.' Dr. Toyoda was so impressed by the Toyota Institute of Technology that he matched Dr. Ty's P1 billion donation -- doubling the total for student beneficiaries

Story 7 -- Mary the Queen Catholic Church in Nanjing: Dr. Ty built and paid for the church single-handedly in thanksgiving for the successful establishment of Metrobank branches in several Chinese cities; CJP used this religious act to approach Dr. Ty about the Manila Cathedral restoration, and Dr. Ty became one of the largest donors

Story 8 -- Invitation to every important gathering: Dr. Ty invited CJP to and expected his presence at every important gathering -- seminars, Masses, inaugurations worldwide, anniversaries, fellowships; that is why CJP chose to come to the wake instead of receiving the FEU Diamond Jubilee Tamaraw Award

Closing spiritual assurance: quoting John 14:1-4 ('In my Father's house are many dwelling places...'); Dr. Ty is 'now enjoying a new life of peace and love in the bosom of the Father'; his qualities to be personified by those left behind: integrity, industry, fairness, generosity, honor, dignity, meekness, thoughtfulness, trustworthiness, discipline and dedication to duty

stances.claim: Dr. Ty's standard of giving -- 10% of total wealth to philanthropy -- is the correct benchmark for a business taipan's social responsibility, far exceeding the corporate standard of 2% of net income. His donation for the Toyota Institute of Technology (P1 billion, matched by Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda) is the single most compelling proof: a total P2 billion for student beneficiaries from an act of individual, not corporate, generosity.
stances.rhetorical_move: 10%-wealth-vs-2%-income benchmark: establishing a higher standard for individual philanthropists vs. corporate CSR norms

stances.claim: Dr. Ty 'never asked from, or was given any favor by, me as a sitting member of the Supreme Court. Our friendship flourished purely on mutual respect and genuine brotherly affection.' This is CJP's highest character attestation -- the absence of judicial favoritism as the proof of integrity in a relationship between a taipan and a sitting justice.
stances.rhetorical_move: no-favor-as-proof-of-integrity: the absence of a thing (judicial favor) as the affirmative evidence of character
stances.confidence: asserted as the most important personal testimony in the eulogy

stances.claim: Dr. Ty's instruction to Alfred after the golf-chastisement -- that excellent golf means too much time on the course and too little at work -- encapsulates his philosophy of leadership by example and total commitment to work: 'What he requires of others, he demands more from himself.' This anecdote is the most compact illustration of the governance principle he embodied.
stances.rhetorical_move: anecdote-as-governance-epitome: the golf-chastisement as the single story that captures the leadership-by-example principle
stances.confidence: asserted as a personal witness account

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered at the first-night wake of Dr. George S.K. Ty on November 24, 2018 -- the night after his death -- this eulogy by CJP was prepared under extraordinary circumstances: Nick Torres called CJP while he was seated beside President Duterte at the San Beda function; CJP texted Cardinal Tagle (in Hong Kong) mid-event; Tagle flew back and celebrated the Mass; CJP skipped the FEU Law Alumni Diamond Jubilee Tamaraw Award (given only once every 50 years) to attend, sending daughter Tet in his stead. He structures the eulogy as nine personal stories, each illuminating a character virtue. Story 1: as Board of Judges chair for Metrobank's Outstanding Teachers search, CJP observed Dr. Ty's soft smile when he asked a teacher why Metrobank would reward her when she gave the bank nothing in return; their friendship 'flourished purely on mutual respect and genuine brotherly affection. He never asked from, or was given any favor by, me as a sitting member of the Supreme Court.' Story 3: CJP praised Alfred's golf game to Dr. Ty at a GT Tower lunch; Dr. Ty summoned Alfred and told him that being a very good golfer was 'bad' -- it meant too much time on the course; 'Since then, I stopped playing with him, lest I slipped and put him in trouble again.' Story 4: Jaime Zobel invited CJP to BPI; Dr. Ty's immediate response by phone: 'Please accept. I fully trust you. I know you will never reveal any business secret.' Story 5: CJP asked if the FLP could buy a used Toyota Innova at APEC discount prices; a week later, Dr. Ty arrived with a brand-new red Innova already registered in FLP's name. Story 6: Dr. Ty pledged 10% of his total wealth to philanthropy (vs. the corporate 2% of net income standard); donated P1 billion for the Toyota Institute of Technology; at a private dinner for retired Toyota Japan Chairman Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda -- who explained that Toyota yielded Philippine majority control because it was the only market where Toyota topped all brands for 27 consecutive years, not even equaled in Japan -- Toyoda was so impressed he matched the P1 billion, doubling the total for students. Story 7: Dr. Ty built the Mary the Queen Catholic Church in Nanjing single-handedly; CJP leveraged this act of faith to approach him for the Manila Cathedral restoration, making him one of its largest donors. The eulogy closes with John 14:1-4 and a 12-virtue inventory -- integrity, industry, fairness, generosity, honor, dignity, meekness, thoughtfulness, trustworthiness, discipline and dedication to duty -- as the legacy to be personified by those left behind.
